card: Adds a cpu_load field to getpeerinfo and a cpu column to bitcoin-cli -netinfo, reporting the CPU time spent in message handling per peer as a proportion of connection duration in per milles. Node operators currently lack visibility into which peers consume the most CPU processing time. The author notes peer CPU monitoring is useful on its own and aids work on peer processing prioritization (#31033). It introduces OS-level thread CPU time measurement on POSIX and Windows.
evidence: Author description: "Monitoring CPU usage is useful on its own. Also related to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31033 [Prioritize processing of peers based on their CPU usage]."
problem: Node operators cannot see which peers consume disproportionate CPU time during message processing, making it difficult to detect resource-intensive or abusive peers and evaluate peer-scheduling policies.
scope_notes: Adds cross-platform per-thread CPU timing utilities in `src/util/time.{h,cpp}` using `clock_gettime(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)` on POSIX and `GetThreadTimes()` on Windows.
summary: Track CPU time spent by the message processing thread on each peer and expose it as a normalized `cpu_load` metric in `getpeerinfo` and `bitcoin-cli -netinfo`. The metric is calculated in per milles (‰) of connection duration using thread CPU time clocks on POSIX and Windows.
